name: Meadow Row
instructions: Wedge one end of a barbell into a landmine base or corner.
Stand perpendicular to the bar, hinging forward with a flat back.
Row the free end to your hip with one hand, elbow driving back.
Lower with control. Named for John Meadows — a thick-back builder.
cues: Pull the elbows to the ribs
longevityNotes: Pull twice as much as you push and your posture will age well. Rowing and pull-up strength are among the best predictors of a capable, pain-free upper body later in life.
overview: An intermediate barbell pull-pattern exercise for the lats. Meadow Row strengthens the back of the upper body, which pays off in posture and shoulder health.
